q1_issues.issue: `AccordingTo` takes a bare event symbol (`sk_fall_1`) as its first argument instead of the sealed proposition P, so the attribution wraps nothing.

Every atom of the reported content (the fall plus the three acquire events, groups and counts) is asserted at top level, violating the non-factive bar that no predication of P may reach top level under 'according to X'.
A scalar-change subject takes `Theme`, not `Patient` ('the temperature fell' -> `(Theme sk_fall_1 sk_temperature_1)`).
The stated figures never attach to the fall eventuality as `MeasureFrom` / `MeasureTo` / `MeasureBy`, so the scalar change carries no values at all and `sk_number_1` holds no measure.
The of-phrase of 'the number of households' is dropped: `sk_number_1` is linked to no household group by any relation.
A participial reduced relative ('households acquiring music') tenses nothing, so `(Past sk_acquire_1)` is unlicensed (same at 12 and 19).

One changing quantity is restructured into three separately asserted past acquire events with three month-stamped household groups, an over-generation the sentence does not state as three occurrences.

q2_gaps: multi-endpoint scalar trajectory ('fell from X in April to Y in May and Z in June') — `MeasureFrom`/`MeasureTo` provide only one start/end pair, with no way to index a value per month
'a high of N' — a peak/extremum descriptor on a scalar start value has no licensed carrier
'the number of N' as a count-valued subject nominal — the of-phrase is neither genitive, partitive, measure nor nominalization-object, so nothing licenses linking the number to the households
notes: Every head used is licensed; the failures are structural — the evidential seal is empty and the scalar-change measure heads are absent. The month/count material is internally consistent but sits at top level where the attribution forbids it.
